newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady in late trade after flotation.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady in late trade after flotation.

text.p: After plunging to a record low against the dollar on Wednesday, the Thai baht was steady late as the two-tiered foreign exchange market limited a baht selloff after the central bank floated the currency, dealers said.
"There were not many transactions today. The continued imposition of the two-tiered market prevented any attack from offshore parties," said one dealer at a European bank.

The baht was quoted at around 27.50/28.50 to the dollar late in domestic markets compared with 27.00/29.00 in the morning, dealers said. In the offshore market, the baht was traded at 28.80/29.60 against 27.00/29.00 in the morning.
Financial authorities announced on Wednesday they had dropped their pegged rate system against a basket of currencies and instead floated the baht and allowed market forces to set exchange rates.
The moves effectively devalued the rate by about 11 percent from its rate at the end of trade on Monday.

The central bank said the two-tiered market -- one offshore and another onshore -- would remain in place although its future would be reviewed. The two-tiered market has been in place since the central bank imposed currency controls amid a speculative attack on the baht in May.
"The selloff on the baht was very limited here because the central bank still imposed the two-tiered market," said one Singapore-based dealer.
Dealers said the market was also confused and investors were waiting to see the central bank's baht-dollar reference rate before taking some actions.
The central bank said a baht-dollar reference would be set daily. The first rate will be set early on Thursday.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 25/35 satangs per dollar late in the domestic market and 35.55 in the offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate surged to 27-30 percent from 13-15 percent late on Monday on strong demand for funds to speculate on the dollar, dealers said.
The interbank rate was unquoted in the morning.
Money and foreign exchange markets were closed on Tuesday for a bank holiday.
